name: Agent credential revocation
description: Revocation claims for identity and credential listings, taken from gap notes. Not documented uses the day the page was read. Omitted means the note has no checked source, or the directory has no gap note and the listing record does not mention revocation. Rows are alphabetical by listing name.
attribution: The Agent Economy credential revocation (https://theagenteconomy.si/data/agent-credential-revocation.json), licensed under CC BY 4.0.

legend.Documented: A cited page states a revoke path.
legend.Not documented: The cited page does not state the fact. The cell includes the day that page was read.
legend.Mixed: The note has both a documented claim and a not documented claim.
legend.Omitted: This directory has no sourced revocation claim for that listing.

rows.name: 1Password for Agents
rows.speed: The credential cache is destroyed when the session ends, when the browser closes, or after a hard cap of nine hours. The page also says you can deny a request.

rows.name: IBM Agent Identity
rows.what: Session. Dynamically generated credential. Agent, by a kill switch in tech preview.
rows.speed: Real time for the session. The same release says dynamically generated credentials expire or can be revoked, and that a kill switch can shut down any agent, and it does not state a time for those.

sources.title: IBM Introduces Identity and Control for AI Agents, Securing Frontier Intelligence for the Enterprise

rows.name: Kite Agent Passport
rows.speed: An approved session lasts until it expires or the budget runs out. A call that revokes an active session before it expires is not documented as of 2026-10-27.

rows.name: ServiceNow AI Passport
rows.speed: The 2026-10-21 release says revocation enforcement can propagate across both layers within approximately one second. The 2026-10-15 release names precision revocation and kill switch capabilities and does not state a time.

sources.title: Socure Launches Agent Intelligence to Bind Every Agent to the Verified Human Behind It
